title: Lab 2 — Quiz 1
subtitle: Culturing Bacteria — culture media and media prep

questions.prompt: What physical state of medium is shown in these flasks?
questions.explanation: Broth is a liquid medium (e.g., TSB, NB). Agar is a solid medium (e.g., TSA, NA).

why.B: Agar media are solid; these flasks contain liquid broth.
why.C: Defined describes chemical composition, not physical state.
why.D: Selective describes function, not physical state.

questions.prompt: This plate contains which type of medium?
questions.explanation: Agar is a solid medium; common examples are Tryptic Soy Agar (TSA) and Nutrient Agar (NA).

why.B: Broth is liquid; this is a Petri plate of agar.
why.C: Complex describes composition, not the physical state shown.
why.D: Reducing media remove oxygen; this question asks about physical state.

questions.prompt: A medium in which the exact ingredients and amounts are known is:
questions.explanation: Defined media: exact ingredients and amounts known; expensive; mostly research labs; rarely medical labs (exception: Citrate Agar).

why.B: Complex media contain basic ingredients but the exact amounts are unknown.
why.C: Enriched is a functional type (adds blood, serum, growth factors).
why.D: General purpose is a functional type for non-fastidious microbes.

questions.prompt: Which defined medium is the exception that IS used in medical labs?
questions.explanation: Defined media are rarely used in medical labs; the exception is Citrate Agar.

why.A: Blood agar is complex (contains blood) — enriched and differential.
why.C: Chocolate agar is an enriched complex medium.
why.D: Nutrient agar is a general purpose complex medium.

questions.prompt: This plate is chocolate agar, which contains special added ingredients. What functional type is it?
questions.explanation: Enriched media add growth factors, serum, blood, metal ions or coenzymes to grow fastidious ('pesky picky eater') microbes. Examples: chocolate agar, blood agar.

why.A: General purpose media (NA, TSA) have only basic nutrients.
why.C: Selective media contain agents that inhibit certain microbes.
why.D: Reducing media contain ingredients that remove oxygen.

questions.prompt: Nutrient agar and tryptic soy agar are examples of which functional type?
questions.explanation: General purpose media support a wide range of non-fastidious microbes: Nutrient Agar, Tryptic Soy Agar, Peptone Broth.

why.B: Enriched examples are chocolate agar and blood agar.
why.C: Differential media show visible differences (e.g., TSI, VRE agar).
why.D: Selective media inhibit certain microbes (e.g., MacConkey, MSA).

questions.prompt: A medium containing agents that inhibit the growth of certain microbes is:
questions.explanation: Selective media inhibit some microbes — a powerful tool for isolation, especially from mixed cultures.

why.A: Differential media show visible differences between organisms.
why.B: Enriched media add nutrients; they don't inhibit growth.
why.D: Defined describes known composition, not function.

questions.prompt: These TSI slants are an example of which functional type of medium?
questions.explanation: Differential media display visible differences (colony color, media color, gas bubbles, liquefaction, antibiotic susceptibility) — a powerful tool for identification.

why.A: TSI doesn't inhibit organisms; it shows visible differences.
why.B: TSI isn't described as adding growth factors for fastidious organisms.

questions.prompt: In the thioglycolate broth tubes shown, where is oxygen concentration highest?

options.text: At the bottom of the tube
In the middle of the tube
At the top of the tube

questions.explanation: Thioglycolate broth (a reducing medium) creates an O2 gradient: top = high, middle = low, bottom = no O2.

why.D: Thioglycolate creates an O2 gradient, not an even level.

questions.prompt: In thioglycolate broth, an organism grows ONLY at the very bottom of the tube. It is a(n):
questions.explanation: Obligate anaerobes grow only where there is no oxygen — the bottom of the thioglycolate tube.

why.A: Obligate aerobes grow only at the top where O2 is high.
why.B: Microaerophiles grow just below the top, where O2 is low.
why.D: Aerotolerant anaerobes grow evenly throughout the tube.

questions.prompt: What are the autoclave settings used to sterilize media?
questions.explanation: An autoclave sterilizes at 121°C, 15 PSI, for 15 minutes. Sterility is tested by endospore survival.

why.B: The settings are 15 PSI for 15 minutes.
why.C: 37°C is an incubation temperature, not sterilization.

questions.prompt: Why are culture media sterilized before use?

options.text: To activate the nutrients in the powder
To prevent contamination and minimize false positives
To lower the pH to the correct level
To remove oxygen from the medium

questions.explanation: Media are sterilized (pre-made or prepared on-site) to prevent contamination and minimize false positives.

why.A: Sterilization kills contaminants; it doesn't activate nutrients.
why.D: That's what reducing media ingredients do.

questions.prompt: How is sterile culture media stored for the short term?
questions.explanation: Short term: refrigeration. Long term: freezing or dehydrating.

questions.prompt: You need 2 L of nutrient broth. The label says: suspend 45 g in 1 L of deionized water. How many grams of powder do you need?

why.A: That divides 45 by 2 instead of multiplying.
why.C: Grams aren't added to liters; multiply 45 g/L × 2 L.

questions.prompt: How is an appropriate pH maintained in culture media?

options.text: The medium is boiled before use
Agar is added to the medium
Buffers are added to the medium
The medium is stored in the refrigerator

questions.explanation: Media must provide nutrients, energy, water, appropriate oxygen and appropriate pH (buffers).

why.A: Boiling dissolves agar; it doesn't control pH.
why.B: Agar solidifies media; it doesn't control pH.
why.D: Refrigeration preserves media; it doesn't set the pH.
